Quarterly Activities Report to 30 June 2026 
30 July 2026 
 
EMC Gold (ASX:EM3; “EMC” or “the Company”) is pleased to provide the following quarterly activities 
report for the period ending 30 June 2026.  
Operational update 
Salave Gold Project 
Following the High Court of Asturias ruling handed down on 1 April 2026 (refer ASX announcement 1 
April 2026), which upheld the Tapia de Casariego Municipal Council's decision not to consider the 
Company's proposed amendment to the municipal urban plan for the Salave Project, the Company has 
continued to advance Salave through ongoing engagement with local and regional stakeholders and 
continued assessment of alternative development pathways. The ruling was procedural in nature and 
did not relate to the technical, environmental or economic merits of the Project. The company is still 
evaluating a drilling program to investigate strategic mineral occurrence and inert sand usage in the 
future.  
WA exploration and tenement holding 
Following the surrender notice submitted in the March 2026 quarter for the 115km2 Ivan Well 
exploration tenement (E69/3818) in Western Australia, the Company lodged its final surrender mineral 
exploration report in April 2026 in accordance with the WA Mining Act 1978.  The company confirms 
that the process is now complete and it holds no other tenure in Western Australia. 
Corporate update 
Board and management changes 
Subsequent to quarter end, the Company announced the appointment of Mr Agne Ahlenius as Chief 
Executive Officer and Executive Director, effective from 6 July 2026, reinforcing EMC Gold's strategic 
focus on Spain and the development of the Salave Gold Project (refer ASX announcement 3 July 
2026). As part of the transition, Non-Executive Director Alberto Lavandeira was appointed Non-
Executive Chairman, and then Executive Chairman Dominic Roberts transitioned to Non-Executive 
Director.  
On 1 April 2026, the Company (EMC Gold Corp.) changed its functional currency from CAD$ to AUD$. 
In determining its functional currency, the Company considered its status as an ASX-listed entity, the 
location of its head office in Australia, the increasing significance of Australian dollar-denominated 
financing, transactions and cash flows, and its predominantly Australian financial reporting obligations. 
The Group’s presentation currency also changed from CAD$ to AUD$ this period, with all amounts 
reported in this Appendix 5B expressed in AUD$. 
 
 
 
For personal use only

 
 
Cash position  
At 30 June 2026, EMC Gold Corporation held AUD$4.420m in cash reserves. 
Related party costs  
During the quarter, the company paid a total of AUD$98,000 to related parties for Director fees and 
salaries.

About EMC Gold  
EMC Gold (ASX:EM3) is an exploration company with a global portfolio of exploration assets. The Company’s flagship project 
is Salave, one of the largest undeveloped gold projects in Europe. Salave is 100 per cent owned by the Company and located 
in the north of Spain in the Principality of Asturias.  
For more information visit www.emcgold.com.au. 
About Salave Gold Project 
The project has a Measured Mineral Resource of 1.03 million tonnes grading 5.59 g/t Au, containing 0.19 million ounces of 
gold; an Indicated Mineral Resource of 7.18 million tonnes grading 4.43 g/t Au, containing 1.02 million ounces of gold, plus 
Inferred Resources totalling 3.12 million tonnes grading 3.47 g/t Au, containing 0.35 million ounces of gold. 
 
The information in this announcement that relates to the Mineral Resource estimate for the Salave project was first released 
by the Company in its news release titled ‘New NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate Increases Resources at Salave’ dated 
31 March 2025.  
 
EMC Gold confirms that it is not aware of any new information or data that materially affects the information included in the 
original announcement and that all material assumptions and technical parameters underpinning the estimate in the previous 
announcement continue to apply and have not materially changed.  
 
A full technical report summarising the Mineral Resource estimate completed by Bara Consulting is available on the 
Company’s web site (www.emcgold.com.au) and posted on SEDAR. In addition to the current Mineral Resource, historical 
exploration work suggests there is the potential for additional mineralisation within EMC Gold’s landholdings.
